question: What does the Catholic Church teach is required for justification — faith alone, or faith and works?

choices.A: Justifying faith is a living faith that includes charity and works — 'faith working through love' (Gal 5:6)
choices.B: Faith alone (sola fide) is sufficient; works are irrelevant to justification
choices.C: Works alone suffice; faith is secondary
choices.D: Neither faith nor works matters — God predestines salvation irrespective of both

teaching.title: Faith, Works, and Justification
teaching.body: The Council of Trent (1547) defined that justification is not by faith alone (contra Luther's sola fide) but by faith that is living — animated by charity and expressed in works. This draws on James 2:24 ('a person is justified by works and not by faith alone'), Galatians 5:6 ('faith working through love'), and Matthew 25:31-46 (judgment by works of mercy). Catholic teaching distinguishes initial justification (received through faith and Baptism) from ongoing growth in righteousness through grace-empowered cooperation.
